newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dow's record close buoys major Asian markets.
newsitem.headline: Dow's record close buoys major Asian markets.

text.p: Wall Street's record overnight close pushed the Hong Kong and Australian markets to record highs again Tuesday and boosted the Tokyo market.
But other Asian markets -- particularly Thailand's -- ignored the Dow's lead, falling on their own domestic political and economic problems.
The Dow ended up 40.99 to close at 6,010 on Monday, the first close ever above the key 6,000 level.

Tokyo stocks surged on the new Wall Street highs as well as speculation that the Liberal Democratic Party may win a majority in the Lower House of parliament in Japan's general election on Sunday, brokers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 jumped 400.68 points or 1.91 percent to close at 21,429.93.
"The Dow closed at over 6,000 and the domestic political picture is coming into focus with the LDP seen at the nucleus," said Yamaichi Securities general manager Tadahiro Kamogawa.

U.S. bullishness spilled over into Hong Kong, where the Hang Seng index recorded its third record closing high in less than a week. Driven higher by continued interest in property and banking stocks, the Hang Seng closed the session at a record 12,490.70, up 160.35 points or 1.30 percent.
"People are enjoying a bit of euphoria at the moment because U.S. interest rates did not go up," said Keith Irving, head of research at HG Asia. Four or five major stocks led the rally.

A Dow-inspired Australian market ended at its second-straight record close. The key All Ordinaries index closed 2.9 points or 0.12 percent higher at 2,366.2, well off its intra-day and life-time high of 2,380.8.

The New Zealand share market rose 57.18 points or 2.53 percent to close at a new 32-month high of 2,321.66 after weaker-than-expected CPI data prompted one of the largest rallies equities have seen this year, brokers said.

Domestic worries reigned in Thailand, where stocks fell for the fifth consecutive trading day on selling by foreigners worried about third quarter earnings and the economy. After dipping below the 900-point mark, the SET index regained some ground to finish 12.96 points or 1.41 percent lower at 905.34.

Seoul shares also tumbled, ending eight straight days of gains, but brokers shrugged off the losses and predicted the market would soon bounce back. The composite stock index lost 13.67 points or 1.62 percent to close provisionally at 828.61.
Taiwan share prices ended slightly lower, down 10.03 points or 0.15 percent at 6,616.38.
